scenes.headline: How a 2.8T model lost three quarters of its experts
scenes.sub: vLLM's pruned Kimi K3.1 Pro, read from its checkpoint.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lopper! The vLLM team cut three quarters of the experts out of Kimi K three point one Pro. Here's how they chose.

scenes.text: In every MoE layer, keep the 224 experts whose router rows have the largest signed sum, and delete the rest, without running any data.
scenes.say: The idea: in every expert layer, keep the experts whose router rows add up highest, and delete the rest, without running the model once.

scenes.title: One MoE layer, before and after

steps.say: A token reaches one of ninety-two expert layers, and the router scores every expert for it.
In the original, it picks sixteen of eight hundred and ninety-six small networks.
The pruned copy keeps two hundred and twenty-four, copied byte for byte, with their router rows.
The router still picks sixteen, so each token does the same work as before. Only memory shrinks.

scenes.title: Why a row sum could mean anything
scenes.text: average logit = w · mu    row sum = w · 1

parts.note: expert's router row against the mean hidden state
parts.say: Averaged over tokens, an expert's router score is its row dotted with the mean hidden state.

parts.note: the same row against all ones
parts.say: The signed sum is the same row dotted with all ones. It only tracks usage if the mean points that way.

scenes.title: Two free scores, two different cuts

steps.label: signed sum
steps.say: Matching router rows shows the shipped set is exactly the top quarter by signed sum, in all ninety-two layers.

steps.label: L1 default
steps.say: The converter's default score would have kept mostly different experts. The two agree barely more than chance.

scenes.title: Checkpoint size, as shipped
scenes.say: The weights fall from about fifteen hundred gigabytes to under five hundred, so eight of the biggest GPUs become two.

scenes.text: A weight-only score can stand in for usage only when the geometry lines up. On a balanced MoE, no score finds much.
scenes.mark: only when the geometry lines up
scenes.say: A data free score only stands in for usage when the geometry lines up. This one is a test fixture, not a smaller Kimi.
Two hundred and twenty-four of eight hundred and ninety-six kept, chosen by a row sum, and every token still runs sixteen.
